page.text:
Although the trio $\{\neg, \land, \lor\}$ is more than adequate to
express every truth function, it is often conceptually clarifying to
introduce specialized connectives for common patterns of thought.

When we wish to capture the everyday 'either-or but not both', we use the
*exclusive disjunction*, written $P \oplus Q$ or $P \text{ xor } Q$. An
exclusive disjunction holds when the two statements have opposite truth
values. Algebraically, it represents the symmetric difference in set
theory and addition modulo $2$ in the field $\mathbb{F}_2$.
